chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:
When the snatching (of the soul) becomes difficult upon him, place him on his prayer-mat in which he used to pray, or on it.

key_terms.النَّزْعُ: The snatching or pulling out of the soul at death
key_terms.مُصَلَّاهُ: His prayer mat or place of prayer
key_terms.يُصَلِّي: He prays (referring to regular prayer practice)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice for placing a dying person who is experiencing difficult death pangs?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on maintaining spiritual continuity at the moment of death by associating the dying with their habitual place of worship. Scholars note that this practice leverages the psychological comfort and divine association of the 'musallah' to ease the soul's transition, reflecting the broader tradition of encouraging good deeds and remembrance during the final breaths.
